fixes.summary: POST /hosts/egress with wait=true answered 200 and ok=true even when the reclaim had not completed on every targeted host, so a caller could not distinguish a complete convergence from a partial one — and the verdict did not come from the same place the rollback path used, so the two could disagree about the same fleet. A partial collection now answers 207 with expected_host_count, missing_hosts and collection_incomplete, and the message carries a WARNING naming how many hosts returned no invocation inside the timeout. The all-hosts form deliberately reports counts WITHOUT a difference set: its DynamoDB enumeration is a snapshot that can include terminated or unmanaged machines and can miss a newly registered one the tag fan-out reaches, so a difference set there would manufacture a permanent 207.
fixes.applies_when: the deployed openclaw-api package's services/egress_admin_service.py does not hash to this kit's copy. Read the package back and compare — a response-shape probe cannot tell an unapplied function from one whose reclaim happened to be complete.

fixes.summary: The edge gate's init_by_lua_block placeholder check was flaky: the same nginx.conf was graded 3/4 and 4/4 across four bb jobs on 2026-08-26, so it could both block an unrelated change and pass when it should have failed. Two causes, both removed: the `awk window | grep -qF` pipeline raced under `set -o pipefail` (grep exits on the first match, awk's next write gets EPIPE and dies non-zero, pipefail fails the whole pipeline and the `&&` skips the count), and the block boundary was guessed from a four-space closing brace, which a nested Lua table closes early. It is now one awk process with brace-pair counting, with three self-checking arms pinning repeatability, block awareness, and that a genuinely missing placeholder still fails.
fixes.applies_when: the object under the served edge bundle prefix does not hash to this kit's copy. This file is read only when the integration suite runs, never on a request path, so there is no running-process state to reconcile.

verifications.action:
set -o pipefail
# EGRESS_TARGET must be an instance carrying BOTH tags the function's SendCommand grant requires:
# Project=openclaw and Role=metal-host. Anything else returns 502 AccessDenied before this branch runs.
: "${EGRESS_TARGET:?set EGRESS_TARGET to a metal-host instance id (tags Project=openclaw, Role=metal-host)}"
: "${OPENCLAW_API_FN:?}"
D=$(mktemp -d)
# The handler accepts an API Gateway proxy v1 event; a rawPath/requestContext.http payload is refused
# with UNSUPPORTED_EVENT_SHAPE (which is itself proof the function is alive).
python3 - "$EGRESS_TARGET" > "$D/payload.json" <<'PY'
import json, sys
print(json.dumps({
    "httpMethod": "POST", "resource": "/hosts/egress", "path": "/hosts/egress",
    "headers": {"content-type": "application/json"},
    "requestContext": {"identity": {"sourceIp": "127.0.0.1"}, "requestId": "oc-v657"},
    "body": json.dumps({"mode": "off", "targets": [sys.argv[1]], "wait": True}),
}))
PY
# --cli-read-timeout 0: with wait=true the handler polls for EGRESS_APPLY_TIMEOUT seconds (default
# 90), which exceeds the CLI's 60s default and would otherwise fail as a read timeout that looks
# like a broken function.
ERR=$(aws lambda invoke --function-name "$OPENCLAW_API_FN" --region "$AWS_REGION" \
  --cli-read-timeout 0 --cli-connect-timeout 10 \
  --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out --payload "file://$D/payload.json" \
  "$D/resp.json" --query FunctionError --output text)
test "$ERR" = "None" || { echo "FAIL: invoke reported FunctionError=$ERR"; exit 1; }
python3 - "$D/resp.json" <<'PY'
import json, sys
r = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
code = r.get("statusCode")
try:
    b = json.loads(r.get("body") or "{}")
except Exception:
    b = {}
msg = str(b.get("message") or "")
print("statusCode=", code, "ok=", b.get("ok"),
      "expected_host_count=", b.get("expected_host_count"),
      "collection_incomplete=", b.get("collection_incomplete"),
      "missing_hosts=", b.get("missing_hosts"))
print("message=", msg[:200])
bad = []
if code == 502:
    bad.append(f"502 — the request never reached the branch under test: {b.get('error')}")
elif code == 400:
    bad.append(f"400 — the payload was refused: {b.get('error')}")
else:
    # The three fields are what this fix adds. They must be PRESENT, whatever the collection outcome
    # of this particular run was. Asserting a specific statusCode transition would be wrong: the
    # pre-fix code already answered 207 when the command itself failed.
    for k in ("expected_host_count", "collection_incomplete", "missing_hosts"):
        if k not in b:
            bad.append(f"the response does not carry {k}; this operation is NOT applied")
    if b.get("expected_host_count") != 1:
        bad.append(f"expected_host_count is {b.get('expected_host_count')!r}, expected 1 for one target")
    # When the collection really was incomplete, the attribution must be complete too.
    if b.get("collection_incomplete") is True:
        if code != 207:
            bad.append(f"collection_incomplete is True but statusCode is {code}, expected 207")
        if b.get("ok") is not False:
            bad.append(f"ok is {b.get('ok')!r} on an incomplete collection, expected False")
        if not b.get("missing_hosts"):
            bad.append("collection_incomplete is True but missing_hosts is empty")
        if "WARNING" not in msg:
            bad.append("collection_incomplete is True but the message carries no WARNING")
    else:
        print("NOTE: the collection completed on this run, so the partial-reclaim attribution was "
              "not exercised end to end. The three fields were still asserted present.")
if bad:
    print("FAIL:", "; ".join(bad)); sys.exit(1)
print("PASS")
PY
verifications.observable: the statusCode and body of POST /hosts/egress (API Gateway proxy v1 event, body {mode, targets, wait}) invoked with one metal-host target and wait=true
verifications.pass_when: the response carries expected_host_count, collection_incomplete and missing_hosts, with expected_host_count equal to the number of targets. When collection_incomplete is True the statusCode must be 207, ok must be False, missing_hosts must name the hosts that did not answer, and the message must carry a WARNING.
verifications.fail_when: any of the three fields is absent — that is what an unapplied function looks like — or collection_incomplete is True while the statusCode is not 207 or missing_hosts is empty. A 502 or 400 is also a failure of the check itself: the request never reached the branch, so it measured nothing. Note that asserting a 200->207 transition would be WRONG: the pre-fix code already answered 207 when the SSM command failed outright; what the fix adds is attribution.

verifications.observable: the branch in the shipped service that decides whether a difference set is computed
verifications.pass_when: the all-hosts form sets missing_hosts to None and collection_incomplete to False, and only the explicit-instance form computes collected_ids
verifications.fail_when: the all-hosts form computes a difference set, which would make 207 permanent on any fleet whose DynamoDB snapshot disagrees with the tag fan-out
